items.title: Traduire l’ambition en action: faire en sorte que le commerce profite aux plus vulnérables( par Xiangchen Zhang) (par
items.description: Nous sommes actuellement à mi-parcours du Programme d'action de Doha des Nations Unies, un programme décennal qui fixe des objectifs commerciaux ambitieux pour aider les pays les moins avancés (PMA) du monde à jouer un rôle plus actif dans le commerce mondial d'ici à 2031. La communauté internationale a fait des progrès constants pour atteindre ces ambitions depuis le lancement du programme en 2022. Dans le même temps, nous avons été confrontés à de fortes turbulences en raison de tensions géopolitiques et de perturbations prolongées. L'environnement extérieur n'a jamais été aussi difficile. Les Membres de l'OMC ont répondu aux appels des PMA en faveur d'une amélioration des possibilités d'accès aux marchés. Aujourd'hui, les exportations des PMA bénéficient d'un accès en franchise de droits aux marchés de destination et de règles d'origine simples et transparentes. Les services et fournisseurs de services des PMA bénéficient également de possibilités dans le domaine du commerce des services. Les PMA disposent aussi de flexibilités en matière de politique pour leur permettre d'intégrer les règles commerciales. Ces dernières années, les Membres de l'OMC ont aussi pris d'importantes mesures pour faciliter une transition sans heurt des pays sortant de la catégorie des PMA. Outre ces progrès, au cours des 20 dernières années, les PMA ont également reçu plus de 223 milliards d'USD au titre de l'aide au développement liée au commerce pour construire des infrastructures et renforcer les secteurs productifs qui les aident à tirer davantage parti du commerce mondial. Les initiatives de renforcement des capacités commerciales continuent d'apporter un soutien indispensable à l'intégration du commerce. Plus tôt cette année, nous avons assisté avec satisfaction au lancement de la troisième phase du Cadre intégré renforcé. Bien que nous ayons des exemples de réussite à partager, les progrès restent inégaux. Les exportations des PMA ne représentent encore que 1,04% des exportations mondiales de marchandises. La part des PMA dans les exportations mondiales de services est de 0,5%, et leur part dans les services fournis par voie numérique est de 0,2%. Trop de personnes vivant dans les PMA n'ont pas encore pleinement exploité leur potentiel commercial. Il faut que cela change. Toutefois, les embûches ne cessent de se multiplier. Si de nouvelles possibilités se profilent, de nouveaux risques apparaissent également. L'année dernière, on a observé une baisse de plus d'un quart de l'aide publique au développement en faveur des PMA. La pression croissante sur les budgets consacrés à l'aide créé une incertitude pour l'Aide pour le commerce, qui représente près d'un cinquième du total de l'aide publique au développement. Nous devons donc faire un choix. Nous pouvons laisser les contraintes budgétaires et l'aggravation des écarts de capacité fragiliser encore plus les économies les plus vulnérables. Ou nous pouvons nous appuyer sur la dynamique créée pour établir des partenariats plus judicieux et aider les PMA à façonner l'avenir du commerce mondial. Cela nécessite d'agir sur trois fronts. 1. Protéger l'aide pour le commerce des demandes concurrentes L'ambition mondiale est de doubler l'Aide pour le commerce en faveur des PMA entre 2018 et 2031. Au cours des cinq dernières années, les décaissements ont augmenté de 1,2% et les engagements ont baissé de 5%. Cette tendance à la baisse est préoccupante. Les PMA peinent également à attirer des financements provenant d'autres sources. En 2024, ils n'ont reçu que 13% du financement du développement lié au commerce non concessionnel, et 7% seulement du financement privé mobilisé pour le commerce. Leur part dans l'investissement étranger direct total est resté aux alentours des 2,5%. Ces chiffres montrent que, dans des contextes vulnérables, le financement privé ne peut pas remplacer le soutien concessionnel. Au contraire, ce sont souvent les ressources concessionnelles qui rendent l'investissement privé possible. Elles nous aident à préparer les projets, à réduire les risques et à créer un environnement propice au commerce et à l'investissement. Dans certains cas, des efforts sont déjà en cours. En Zambie, la coopération avec la Chine a permis de construire des usines de transformation de farine de maïs, ce qui a augmenté la valeur ajoutée locale et permis de créer de meilleurs emplois. Au Togo, les améliorations apportées dans le secteur du soja – y compris grâce au soutien fourni par le Cadre intégré renforcé – ont contribué à attirer 25 millions d'USD pour une installation moderne de transformation de fèves de soja. Par conséquent, la réponse ne consiste pas à choisir entre l'aide et l'investissement. Elle consiste en une aide qui mobilise l'investissement. Il ne s'agit pas d'un financement public ou privé. Il s'agit d'un partenariat qui tire le meilleur profit des deux. Une réduction du soutien ciblé pour le commerce pourrait compromettre des années de progrès durement acquis. 2. Mettre l'accent sur les écarts de connaissances en matière de politique commerciale Environ 98% de l'Aide pour le commerce en faveur des PMA est destinée aux infrastructures et aux secteurs de production. Et seulement 2% sont destinés à la politique et à la réglementation commerciales sous la forme d'un soutien qui contribue à la négociation et à la mise en œuvre des règles commerciales. Des programmes ciblés – qui vont du Programme de la Chine pour les PMA au soutien quotidien que le Fonds pour la promotion du commerce du Royaume-Uni offre au Groupe des PMA de l'OMC – ont aidé les PMA à participer plus efficacement aux travaux de l'OMC. La participation accrue des PMA à l'OMC a produit des résultats. Depuis 2022, les Membres de l'OMC ont adopté quatre décisions en réponse aux demandes des PMA. Il s'agit notamment de deux décisions visant à faciliter une transition sans heurt des pays sortant de la catégorie des PMA – une priorité centrale pour le Groupe des PMA. L'assistance technique de l'OMC a également joué un rôle important. Depuis 2022, plus de 16 600 participants originaires de 42 PMA ont reçu une formation sur les règles de l'OMC et leur mise en œuvre. Ces programmes de soutien pour le commerce, modestes mais d'un grand impact, permettent aux pays d'acquérir les connaissances nécessaires pour négocier, des capacités de mise en œuvre et la confiance pour diriger. Or, ce sont précisément ces programmes que la réduction des budgets d'aide pourrait mettre en péril. 3. Repenser les stratégies de négociation De grands groupes de Membres ont discuté de nouvelles règles, mais la participation des PMA à ces discussions a été en demi-teinte. Par exemple, sur les 70 Membres qui font partie de l'Accord sur le commerce électronique, qui vise à assurer un environnement favorable au commerce numérique, 5 seulement sont des PMA. Dans le même temps, nous constatons davantage d'intérêt de la part des PMA dans la facilitation de l'investissement, 27 PMA ayant accédé à l'Accord sur la facilitation de l'investissement pour le développement. Depuis trop longtemps, les PMA se sont concentrés sur leurs intérêts défensifs – comment se protéger contre les nouvelles obligations et les difficultés de mise en œuvre. Ces préoccupations sont réelles. Mais des efforts supplémentaires sont nécessaires pour aider les PMA à identifier leurs priorités commerciales émergentes et les possibilités qu'elles offrent. Ils ne doivent donc plus se demander quels risques ils doivent éviter, mais plutôt quelles possibilités ils doivent saisir. À l'heure où les Membres réfléchissent à la manière de réformer l'OMC, donner à chaque pays les moyens de contribuer aux négociations sur l'avenir du commerce est peut-être la meilleure approche. Des partenariats plus solides en matière de soutien pour le commerce resteront essentiels pour ces efforts. Si vous souhaitez explorer d'autres idées sur la manière d'aider les PMA à jouer un rôle plus actif dans le commerce mondial, venez participer à la conversation lors de l'Examen global à l'OMC, le 29 octobre. Par Xiangchen Zhang, Directeur général adjoint, OMC

items.title: 2027: I’ve handed everything over to God, says INEC chairman
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, has said he has handed everything over to God as he confronts the responsibility of conducting the 2027 general election. Amupitan, who spoke on Wednesday at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026 in Abuja, said his faith in God remained his anchor amid the enormous demands of his office. He said, “I’m being reminded of the enormity of the task on me. I’m also encouraged by the word of God, which is, ‘Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.’ So that has been my anchor. “And sometimes people say, ‘You are not bothered.’ I said, I’ve handed over everything to God.” The INEC chairman spoke at the forum organised by Yiaga Africa, which had as its theme, “Safeguarding the 2027 General Election in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.” Addressing participants, Amupitan assured Nigerians that artificial intelligence would not determine the outcome of the 2027 general election, insisting that the power to choose the country’s leaders rested with the electorate. He said, “No, algorithms will not and must never decide the 2027 votes. Algorithms will not decide the vote because the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people.” According to him, while AI would influence the information voters receive, electoral logistics and political communication, the technology must remain a tool for strengthening democracy rather than undermining it. “Our task, therefore, at this forum and within the Commission is to ensure that AI remains a servant of democracy, not its master,” he said. Amupitan said the 2027 general election would involve more than 103 million registered voters across 176,846 polling units in the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory. He noted that the scale of the exercise, coupled with difficult terrain, insecurity and poor network coverage in some communities, posed significant logistical challenges for the commission. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had completed 10 of the 14 major activities on its election timetable, despite the strict timelines prescribed by the Electoral Act 2026. He added that INEC had procured and begun receiving additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System devices to strengthen its technological capacity ahead of the polls. Amupitan also said the commission had digitised its candidate nomination process through the INEC Candidate Nomination Portal, which had processed more than 15,000 nominations across 22 political parties. He further disclosed that INEC had introduced online voter registration and was implementing a decentralised, multi-phase Permanent Voter Card collection exercise nationwide. On the use of AI in election administration, the INEC chairman said the technology could improve the deployment of election materials and personnel through predictive modelling and geospatial analysis. According to him, AI-driven systems can analyse traffic patterns, weather forecasts, road conditions and security incidents to determine suitable routes for transporting electoral materials to polling units. He said such systems could also provide early warnings of weather-related disruptions and help the commission identify logistical challenges before election day. On electoral integrity, Amupitan said biometric voter accreditation and electronic transmission of polling-unit results had helped address vulnerabilities associated with manual accreditation and arbitrary manipulation of results. He added that AI could assist in auditing uploaded polling-unit result sheets by identifying mathematical inconsistencies, unusual entry patterns and discrepancies in image quality. However, he stressed that human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring election results, while AI could provide additional support in detecting anomalies. The INEC chairman said the commission would continue to work with civil society organisations, technology firms, regulatory bodies and security agencies to harness the benefits of AI while addressing potential threats to the electoral process. He maintained that the ultimate responsibility of electoral stakeholders was to ensure that technological advancements strengthened democratic institutions without compromising the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. items.title: Après Sebta, Felipe VI se rend à Melilla
items.description: Après s’être rendu hier dans la ville de Sebta occupée, le roi d’Espagne Felipe VI est arrivé ce mercredi à Melilla, elle aussi occupée, dans une démarche inédite depuis son accession au trône de ce pays ibérique. Cette visite revêt une portée politique importante et remet en lumière la question des enclaves marocaines occupées, qui constituent un point de contact complexe entre les continents africain et européen. Accompagné de son épouse, la reine Letizia, le souverain espagnol a été accueilli chaleureusement par des milliers de citoyens espagnols résidant dans la ville occupée. Une foule nombreuse s’est rassemblée dans les principales rues et places, dans une ambiance festive ponctuée de slogans de soutien. Cette mobilisation porte notamment un message adressé au Maroc, visant à réaffirmer le refus de Madrid de voir sa « souveraineté » sur cette ville occupée remise en question. La visite de Felipe VI a débuté par un accueil au siège de l’Assemblée de Melilla (Palacio de la Asamblea), en présence de Juan José Imbroda, président du gouvernement local de la ville, qui a remis au roi la « clé d’or de la ville » dans la salle dorée. Une soixantaine de personnalités représentant les différentes autorités et institutions locales, judiciaires et militaires, ainsi que des représentants religieux, ont assisté à cette cérémonie. Selon le programme annoncé par le palais royal espagnol, le souverain doit également visiter l’école publique Pintor Eduardo Morillas, qui accueille plus de 900 élèves et compte 79 enseignants. Cette visite lui permettra de découvrir les salles de classe et un projet innovant destiné à accompagner les élèves atteints d’autisme. Le déplacement doit s’achever par une rencontre avec quelque 400 personnalités représentant les différentes composantes de la société de Melilla. À travers cette tournée sur le terrain, qui a conduit Felipe VI à Sebta et à Melilla en l’absence du Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez, la monarchie espagnole entend réaffirmer la « souveraineté espagnole » sur ces deux enclaves occupées. Cette démarche intervient notamment après la polémique suscitée en Espagne par l’entrée massive de migrants en situation irrégulière à Sebta, à la fin du mois de juillet dernier, ainsi que par les vives critiques adressées au gouvernement et palais elle-même. De l’autre côté, cette visite a provoqué une vague de protestations dans les milieux associatifs marocains. Ceux-ci y voient une démarche provocatrice susceptible d’entraver les efforts visant à construire un partenariat stratégique équilibré entre Rabat et Madrid, fondé sur le respect mutuel. Ils dénoncent également une tentative de consolider une réalité coloniale que le Maroc a historiquement rejetée et dont il continue de réclamer la fin, en vue de recouvrer sa souveraineté sur ces deux enclaves. Le ministre de la Justice du gouvernement sortant, Abdellatif Ouahbi, avait déjà suscité une vive polémique en Espagne après avoir affirmé, lors d’un entretien accordé à la presse en août dernier, que le Maroc n’entendait pas renoncer à ses revendications concernant les deux villes occupées. Il avait proposé la mise en place d’un mécanisme bilatéral permettant d’aborder leur avenir dans le cadre de négociations entre le Maroc et l’Espagne. The post Après Sebta, Felipe VI se rend à Melilla appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Air Algérie suspend les ventes de billets vers l’Arabie Saoudite
items.description: La situation est tendue au niveau des aéroports saoudiens à la suite de frappes des rebelles Houthis du Yémen. Plusieurs compagnies ont déjà suspendu leurs vols vers l’Arabie Saoudite. Quid d’Air Algérie ? L’aéroport de Riyad a été visé par une série d’attaques aériennes, dont l’une a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés le 10 octobre dernier. L’attaque est la plus meurtrière que le pays ait connue depuis 2015. Arabie Saoudite : plusieurs compagnies aériennes suspendent leurs vols Outre l’aéroport de Riyad, les aéroports d’Abha et de Dammam ont été également ciblés. Les attaques ont été revendiquées par les rebelles Houthis qui ont assuré que les aéroports saoudiens n'étaient « pas sûrs », hormis ceux de la Mecque et de Médine, les deux villes saintes du Royaume. Dans la foulée, plusieurs compagnies aériennes ont suspendu leurs vols au départ et à destination de l’Arabie Saoudite. C’est le cas de Qatar Airways, qui n’a pas donné de date de reprise de ses vols, mais aussi d'Etihad qui a annulé ses liaisons vers Dammam et Riyad au moins jusqu’au 19 octobre, mais aussi avec Djeddah jusqu’au 15 octobre. Air France aussi a annoncé la suspension de ses vols vers Riyad jusqu’au 31 octobre, tandis que la compagnie aérienne allemande, Lufthansa, a suspendu ses vols vers la capitale saoudienne jusqu’au 16 octobre. Suspension des vols vers l'Arabie Saoudite : que fera Air Algérie ? Du côté d’Air Algérie, aucune annonce n’a été faite à ce sujet. La compagnie aérienne nationale ne dessert pas l’aéroport de Riyad, ni celui de Dammam, les seuls touchés par les frappes houthis jusque-là, mais elle assure des vols réguliers vers Djeddah et Médine, au départ des aéroports d’Alger et d’Oran et de Constantine. Air Algérie n’a pas annoncé de suspension de vols vers les deux aéroports saoudiens qu'elle dessert, mais elle ne propose plus désormais de réservations vers ces deux destinations sur son site Web, fait savoir le site spécialisé Voyages et Diaspora ( VVA ). L’article Air Algérie suspend les ventes de billets vers l’Arabie Saoudite est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Faceless taxman
items.description: IN June 2026, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved a New Tax Operating Model — launched this month — to adopt a centralised, digital ‘faceless’ system that replaces individual tax officers with one that has sweeping authority over taxpayers’ cases. Cases will be allocated via an algorithm, and the hearings will move online. The goal is to end direct, discretionary contact between officials and taxpayers, which has long been accused of harassment, bribery, and outright collusion. It remained only a policy announcement until the Finance Bill 2026 , which took effect on July 1, 2026, gave the model legal force by amending the Sales Tax Act, the Income Tax Ordinance, and the Customs Act. But the amendments did not create any new or required procedural rights for taxpayers specific to the faceless context and routed existing appeal mechanisms, adopting whatever weaknesses and strengths they already had. This reform responds to a serious problem, as the FBR cites in support of the plan: 8,697 individuals holding a combined Rs750 billion in bank deposits reported zero income. Centralisation of audit selection through an algorithm is a defensible response to this reality. But this reform leaves one question unanswered: if a business is assessed, penalised, or denied a refund under an algorithmic case allocation system, what does the business get in return? What does due process look like when an anonymous unit makes the decision? It is tempting to view a ‘faceless’ system as the equivalent of a ‘fair’ system. This improvement is genuine and welcome, as most complaints filed on the Pakistan Citizen’s Portal show just how badly things work for ordinary taxpayers. Digitising the process is reasonable. But discretion does not disappear when a human officer is replaced with a case-routing algorithm or by a distant unit. It moves from visible to invisible discretion — the latter is embedded in a data model and the design choices of whoever built the Central Data Hub. Face-to-face corruption can be witnessed, but corruption embedded in a black-box algorithm can be denied and hidden. Corruption embedded in an algorithm can remain hidden. If Pakistan wants this reform actually to deliver justice rather than merely relocate discretion, several elements must be added. They should not be optional extras; they should form the core of the reform. The right to information and reasons: A specific and substantive explanation must be given to every business that is assessed by the National Assessment Wing about why a demand was raised. The final assessment order must lay out the facts and reasoning in enough detail for the taxpayer to contest it rather than guess at it. A real and timely right to appeal: The reform proposes that the FBR will retain the authority to move tax appeals to a faceless format in phases. The sequencing matters, because an appeals system that remains slow, paper-based, and subject to the same information asymmetries as the assessment stage will reproduce the old system at one level up. Contestability of the algorithm, not just the outcome: It is essential to assess whether independent oversight bodies, such as the Finance Committee, can examine whether the model is biased and systematically flags certain sectors, cities, or business sizes unfairly. An algorithm that cannot be audited by anyone outside the tax authorities is simply discretion in technical disguise. Proportionate treatment of small businesses: While a large corporate taxpayer is well-equip­ped and resourced enough to navigate a digital, document-heavy, and faceless system, a small trader who already struggles with e-filing or an entrepreneur who doesn’t have enough funds is not. If the Field Operation Wing’s facilitation role is under-resourced compared with its enforcement role, the new system will benefit only taxpayers who can afford professional representation. This will perpetuate the same unevenness and continuity of injustice that the reform was meant to fix. None of this argues against digitising the tax administration, but Pakistan does not merely need a faceless tax administration. It needs a new system with transparency obligations and accountability that a human face, however imperfect, is in a position to provide. The new system also needs to build enforceable rights for the taxpayer. This will determine whether the reform is remembered as genuine modernisation or as the moment when discretion in Pakistan’s tax system simply learnt to hide better. The writer is a law student at Lums with research interests in gender, AI and public policy. Published in Dawn, October 14th, 2026

items.title: NHRC laments rising cases of rights violations, receives 338,810 petitions
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Wednesday expressed concern over the increasing cases of rights violations in the country, revealing that it received a total of 338,810 complaints in September alone. According to the Commission, the majority of petitions lodged before it were from the North-Central geopolitical zone, with most cases originating from Benue, Plateau and Niger states. The Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, said the Commission’s human rights dashboard showed an increase of 40,867 complaints, approximately 14 per cent, compared with the 297,943 recorded in August. “This figure is significant and calls for sustained attention. While an increase in complaints may reflect greater public awareness of human rights and improved access to the Commission’s services, it equally underscores the enormous responsibility placed upon the Commission and other duty-bearers to respond effectively to allegations of violations. “Our concern must therefore extend beyond the number of complaints received to the quality of investigations conducted, the remedies secured for victims and the preventive measures put in place to address recurring violations. “The human rights landscape in Nigeria during September 2026 continued to present serious challenges, particularly in relation to the right to life, personal liberty, human dignity, security of persons and the protection of vulnerable populations. “Insecurity remained a major concern, with reports of killings, kidnappings and attacks on communities in different parts of the country. “Of particular concern were the continuing reports of mass abductions in Niger State, where families and communities expressed anguish over the prolonged captivity of their loved ones. The Commission reiterates that the protection of life and property is a fundamental obligation of the State. “We therefore call on relevant security agencies to intensify efforts towards securing affected communities, rescuing abducted persons and ensuring that perpetrators of these crimes are brought to justice,” Ojukwu, SAN, added. He said the Commission was also concerned about the persistent vulnerability of women and children to sexual and gender-based violence, exploitation, abuse and other forms of discrimination. “These violations demand stronger preventive mechanisms, survivor-centred responses, effective investigations and improved access to justice. “In this regard, we welcome the national stakeholders’ engagement held in September on the review of the Child Rights Act, 2003. “This presents an important opportunity to strengthen Nigeria’s child protection framework and address gaps in the prevention of violence, exploitation and abuse against children. “We urge relevant authorities to ensure that these reform efforts translate into stronger institutions, adequate resources and practical protection for children, particularly those in vulnerable and underserved communities. “The Commission remains committed to improving its monitoring and reporting mechanisms, strengthening investigations and complaints resolution, and ensuring that its findings inform policies and institutional reforms. “Our objective is not merely to document violations after they occur, but to contribute to a system where violations are prevented, victims obtain justice and public institutions are held accountable,” the NHRC boss added, even as he called for increased funding for the Commission. Meanwhile, a Special Human Rights Adviser to the Commission, Mr. Hillary Ogbonna, who gave a breakdown of some of the cases in the dashboard, said a total of 208 killings by non-state actors and 210 kidnappings were recorded in September. He said the Commission visited 113 detention centres across the federation and issued 56 summons to the police over cases of human rights abuses. items.title: Enugu police arrest 182 suspects, rescue 31 kidnap victims
items.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU — The Enugu State Police Command says it has arrested 182 suspects, rescued 31 kidnapped victims and recovered 57 firearms, including 13 AK-47 rifles, since the establishment of its Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) in April 2026. The Commissioner of Police, Mamman Bitrus Giwa, disclosed this on Wednesday while presenting the unit’s operational scorecard during its formal launch by the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, at the VCRU headquarters in Golf Estate, Enugu. Giwa said the suspects were arrested for offences including armed robbery, kidnapping, unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition, cultism, and drug and substance trafficking. He added that many of the suspects had been prosecuted. The police commissioner said the unit also recovered 669 rounds of assorted live ammunition and 44 vehicles, comprising cars, tricycles and motorcycles, alongside other exhibits. The Inspector-General of Police, represented by the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 13, Miller Gajere Dantawaye, described the establishment of the VCRU as a strategic initiative to strengthen intelligence-driven policing, prevent violent crime and protect lives and property. Disu charged personnel of the unit to uphold professionalism, discipline, accountability and respect for human rights in the discharge of their duties. He also commended Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, for providing vehicles and supporting security infrastructure across the state. Giwa explained that the VCRU comprised specialised sections responsible for tackling armed robbery, terrorism and related offences, kidnapping, cultism and drug trafficking. He said other sections handled operational monitoring, professional conduct oversight and media liaison. The commissioner reaffirmed the command’s commitment to combating violent crime and safeguarding lives and property, while acknowledging the state government’s continued support for security operations. Speaking on behalf of the VCRU State Civilian Oversight Board, a representative of civil society organisations, Larry Ogwuego, commended the Inspector-General for establishing the unit and promoting intelligence-led operations and respect for human rights. Ogwuego assured that the board would discharge its oversight responsibilities to promote accountability and incorporate community feedback into the unit’s activities. The launch, held at the VCRU headquarters in Golf Estate, Enugu, was attended by senior police officers, Vincent Onyeabor, Special Assistant to the Governor, and members of the State Civilian Oversight Board representing traditional institutions, the legal profession, the Police Community Relations Committee, the media and youth groups. items.title: Exploitation aurifère : Boya Sa s’installe à Dakar
items.description: La filiale sénégalaise du géant minier Fortuna Mining a officiellement inauguré ses nouveaux locaux mercredi dernier, marquant son passage stratégique de l'exploration à l'exploitation commerciale de l’or. C’est un tournant décisif pour l’industrie extractive sénégalaise. Après une phase d’exploration minutieuse, BOYA SA, filiale du Groupe Fortuna Mining, s’apprête à lancer l’exploitation commerciale et le développement de ses gisements d’or au Sénégal, notamment à travers le projet Diamba Sud de la région de Kédougou, récemment renforcé par l’acquisition du projet Boto. Pour matérialiser cette transition et affirmer sa présence institutionnelle, la direction a inauguré son nouveau siège à Dakar. Un investissement colossal compris entre 150 et 170 milliards de fCfa a déjà été injecté pour la construction de la mine, promettant des retombées économiques majeures pour le pays. Présidant la cérémonie, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Cheikhou Oumar Seck, a salué cette étape importante qui concrétise le soutien de l’Etat au secteur privé national et international. Il a profité de l’occasion pour décliner les priorités de la vision minière nationale. « La politique de l'Etat dans le secteur des mines se résume en deux principaux points ; la souveraineté sur nos ressources et la transformation locale », a-t-il martelé. Evoquant les avancées significatives enregistrées depuis le mois de juin sur plusieurs projets aurifères, le ministre a également annoncé la stabilisation imminente du cadre légal. Le nouveau code minier est en phase finale de bouclage, tandis que le décret portant sur le fonds de réhabilitation et celui lié au contenu local ont été finalisés. Au-delà de l'or, cette dynamique de transformation locale touchera également l'orpaillage artisanal, les phosphates pour la souveraineté alimentaire, et le fer avec pour cible ultime l’émergence d'une industrie sidérurgique lourde. Pour le secteur privé, cette inauguration dépasse le cadre architectural. Selon le président de la Chambre des mines du Sénégal, Ousmane Mbaye, ce nouveau siège est un véritable « point d'ancrage, un espace de décision, de dialogue et surtout un signal fort de confiance dans le potentiel de notre pays ». Saluant la création d’emplois et les achats locaux déjà générés par le groupe, il a exhorté à rompre définitivement avec la simple logique d'extraction brute. « Notre ambition commune doit être de passer progressivement d'une logique d'extraction à une logique de création de valeur en renforçant les capacités nationales et en consolidant les partenariats avec les entreprises sénégalaises », a-t-il plaidé. Représentant le Comité National de l'ITIE, le président Thialy Faye a souligné quatre piliers cardinaux pour le développement des projets dans la zone stratégique du Sénégal oriental à savoir le contenu local, l’emploi qualifié, le développement territorial et la transparence financière (divulgation des contrats, des revenus et de la propriété effective). « Nous encourageons Fortuna et Boya à inscrire leur développement dans une démarche fondée sur la transparence et le dialogue. L'ITIE n'est pas là pour se substituer aux administrations, mais pour créer les conditions d’un dialogue informé et constructif », a-t-il conclu. Samba DIAMANKA

items.title: Bilateral security cooperation comes under discussion as Russian interior minister meets CDF Munir
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev called on Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi on Wednesday, where both sides stressed the importance of bolstering defence cooperation between Islamabad and Moscow. Kolokoltsev arrived in Pakistan on Monday on a four-day visit at the invitation of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, marking the first instance of a Russian interior minister visiting Pakistan. According to a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), both sides discussed matters of mutual interest and the regional security landscape, with emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation. “They underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia,” the statement said. It added that CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to “deepen its longstanding relations with Russia and expand tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain”. Kolokoltsev also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability, acknowledging the professionalism and sacrifices of Pakistani forces in the fight against terrorism, the statement concluded. Pakistan, Russia agree to finalise extradition treaty Earlier in the day, Pakistan and Russia agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and pledged to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in preventing organised crime and exchanging information. The understanding was reached during a meeting between Naqvi and Kolokolstev in Islamabad. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks, the interior ministry said in a statement. Naqvi, during the meeting, said the proposed MoU on prevention of organised crime would be an important milestone in cooperation between the two countries. The two sides pledged to enhance mutual cooperation in areas of shared interests as they agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and an agreement on the exchange of criminals. Both sides resolved to promote cooperation in areas of mutual interest and decided to ensure early implementation of a readmission agreement, according to the statement. They also agreed to enhance cooperation between the Anti-Narcotics Force and relevant Russian institutions. It was agreed in the meeting that working groups from the interior ministries of both countries would soon visit each other. The two sides also discussed sending skilled manpower from Pakistan to Russia and facilitating visa acquisition for tourists and the business community, as per the statement. They agreed to enhance cooperation for the prevention of cybercrime between the National Police Academy and the Russian Police Academy, the statement said. Naqvi said easing the visa regime would increase people-to-people contact between the two countries. He also expressed desire to benefit from Russia’s experiences in curbing cybercrime. He further noted that at present, 1,300 Pakistani students were studying in Russia and Pakistan wanted more students to study there. Russian Interior Minister Kolokolstev, for his part, said joint measures were essential for the prevention of all organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling, and illegal migration. He said Russia had brought a 33 per cent reduction in cybercrime through effective measures. The meeting was attended by Minister of State Tallal Chaudhry, the Russian ambassador in Pakistan, special and additional secretaries to interior and other senior officials. In recent years, Pakistan and Russia have significantly strengthened their economic ties, driven by mutual necessity. In January, Russian President Vladimir Putin had said Moscow’s relations with Pakistan were “ genuinely mutually beneficial ” and that it maintained close ties with Islamabad. Last July, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk called Pakistan and Russia “ natural allies ”, stressing that Putin viewed Islamabad as an important strategic partner in the areas of economy and energy. Following Western sanctions related to the Ukraine conflict , Moscow turned toward new energy outlets, while Islamabad simultaneously sought more affordable fuel sources to reduce national import expenses. This diplomatic shift culminated in 2023, when Pakistan officially integrated Russian crude oil into its energy portfolio.

items.title: Nigeria secures 172 votes for UN Human Rights Council seat
items.description: By Favour Ulebor Nigeria has been elected to the United Nations Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term after securing 172 votes in an election conducted by the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The Federal Government announced the election in a statement issued on Wednesday and signed by the Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Oluwafemi Adeniyi. According to the statement, Nigeria was elected alongside 14 other countries to serve a three-year term beginning January 1, 2027, and ending December 31, 2029. The 47-member council is responsible for promoting and protecting human rights globally and strengthening international cooperation on human rights issues. The Federal Government expressed appreciation to United Nations member states for supporting Nigeria’s candidature. It also reaffirmed the country’s commitment to dialogue, cooperation and mutual respect in advancing the council’s mandate. “The Federal Government of Nigeria wishes to announce Nigeria’s election to the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term, having secured 172 of 181 votes during the Council’s election held on 13 October 2026 by the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA),” the statement said. “Nigeria was elected alongside fourteen other countries to serve a three-year term commencing on 01 January 2027 and ending on 31 December 2029.” The government said Nigeria looked forward to working closely with other council members to strengthen international efforts towards the promotion and protection of human rights. It added that the country remained committed to constructive multilateral engagement and initiatives that uphold human dignity, justice and fundamental freedoms. Nigeria is expected to begin its three-year membership in January 2027, joining other elected members in addressing human rights concerns and promoting international cooperation on the protection of fundamental rights. items.description: The number of jobs advertised in selected print and online media, which partially gauges labour demand in the economy, increased in July 2026 relative to what was observed in the corresponding period a year ago. In total, 3,578 job adverts were recorded in July 2026, the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report has stated. This is compared with 2,703 for the same period in 2025, indicating an increase of 32.4% year-on-year. Conversely, on a month-on-month basis, the number of job vacancies in July 2026 marginally declined by 1.4% from the 3,629 jobs advertised in June 2026. Cumulatively, for the first seven months of 2026, the total number of advertised jobs increased by 8.2% to 23,052 from the 21,307 recorded during the same period in 2025. Private Sector Pension Contributors Meanwhile, the total number of private-sector SSNIT contributors, which partially gauges employment conditions, improved by 6.1% to 1,178,451 in July 2026. This is compared with 1,110,976 for the same period in 2025. On a month-on-month basis, the total number of private-sector SSNIT contributors remained largely unchanged from the 1,176,723 individuals recorded in June 2026.

items.title: Nigeria seeks more Hungary scholarship slots for students
items.description: … Ambassador Braimah asks Tempus Foundation to increase allocation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Nigeria’s Ambassador to Hungary, Engr. Abass Braimah, has called for an increase in the number of scholarship slots allocated to Nigerian students under the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme. Braimah made the appeal on Tuesday during a working visit to the headquarters of Tempus Public Foundation in Budapest, Hungary, describing the current allocation of 50 slots to Nigeria as inadequate for a country with a large population. The ambassador urged the foundation to increase the allocation to enable more qualified Nigerian students to benefit from the programme. He also encouraged eligible Nigerians to apply when the application window opens in November 2026. In a statement issued by his office on Wednesday, Braimah said the visit was part of the Nigerian Embassy’s efforts to strengthen bilateral relations between Nigeria and Hungary and support Nigerian students pursuing their studies in the European country. He was accompanied on the visit by the Deputy Head of Mission and Minister Plenipotentiary, Mrs Vivienne Ekwora Ogonyi. The delegation was received by the Director-General of Tempus Public Foundation, Mr Péter Tordai, and the Director of Study in Hungary, Ms Orsolya Jánosik. According to the statement, discussions focused on strengthening educational cooperation between both countries, particularly through the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme, which provides opportunities for Nigerian students to study at Hungarian universities. The embassy said the engagement formed part of its broader efforts to deepen Nigeria-Hungary relations and promote educational opportunities for Nigerian students in Hungary. items.title: KNUST to receive 2,000 additional laptops for One Million Coders Programme
items.description: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is expected to receive an additional 2,000 laptops to expand access to digital skills training under the government’s One Million Coders Programme (OMCP). The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, announced the planned provision during a working visit to the university as part of his tour of the Ashanti Region to assess the implementation of the programme and identify expansion opportunities. The additional laptops will support the establishment of 40 new learning centres on the KNUST campus, increasing the number of centres from the existing 10 to 50. The university initially received 500 laptops to equip the first 10 centres under the initiative. During the visit, the Minister toured some of the learning centres and interacted with students to assess their experiences with the programme. He also encouraged greater participation as the government seeks to widen access to digital education and equip more young people with skills relevant to the changing employment landscape. The expansion is expected to make digital skills training more accessible to students and other prospective learners within the university community. It will also provide additional opportunities for beneficiaries to develop competencies that can support innovation, entrepreneurship and employment in Ghana’s growing digital economy. Mr George further disclosed that the Ministry was exploring opportunities to extend the programme to other tertiary institutions in the Ashanti Region, including Kumasi Technical University. Such partnerships could broaden the initiative’s reach beyond KNUST and enable more students to benefit from structured digital skills training. The working visit forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to monitor the implementation of the One Million Coders Programme, identify operational challenges and determine areas where additional resources and institutional partnerships could improve its reach. The programme is designed to equip Ghanaians with relevant digital skills to enhance their employability, support innovation and prepare them to participate more effectively in the digital economy. The planned provision of the additional laptops is expected to strengthen KNUST’s capacity to deliver the training, although the Ministry did not specify a delivery date for the new equipment in the announcement. One Million Coders Programme: Samuel Nartey George targets 50 learning centres at KNUST The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has announced plans to increase the number of One Million Coders Programme (OMCP) learning centres at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) from 10 to 50, in a major expansion of digital skills training at the university. The expansion will be supported by an additional 2,000 laptops to be provided to KNUST, building on the initial allocation of 500 laptops used to establish the first 10 learning centres. The move is expected to extend access to technology-enabled training and provide more learners with opportunities to acquire digital competencies. Mr George announced this during a working visit to KNUST as part of his tour of the Ashanti Region to assess progress under the government’s flagship digital skills initiative. The visit included tours of some learning centres and engagements with students to understand how the programme is operating on campus and identify opportunities to improve participation. The proposed expansion will add 40 learning centres to the existing facilities, potentially increasing the university’s capacity to accommodate more students and other prospective participants. The Minister also disclosed that the Ministry was exploring possible partnerships with other tertiary institutions in the region, including Kumasi Technical University, to extend the programme beyond KNUST. The move would create opportunities for more students to access digital skills training without relying solely on the facilities available at one institution. The One Million Coders Programme is intended to equip Ghanaians with practical digital skills that can improve employability, promote entrepreneurship and support the development of a workforce capable of responding to the demands of an increasingly technology-driven economy. The initiative also forms part of the government’s broader digital transformation agenda, which places emphasis on expanding access to technology, strengthening digital capacity and preparing young people for opportunities in the digital economy. The Ministry’s engagement with KNUST is expected to inform further decisions on the programme’s implementation and expansion in the Ashanti Region. However, the announcement did not indicate when the additional laptops would be delivered or when the 40 new learning centres would become operational.

items.title: Nigeria woos foreign investors with 65 projects worth $78.5bn
items.description: *Energy, transport account for $61.4bn; 17 mega-projects require $72.3bn *Foreign investors to enjoy 100% foreign ownership, tax incentives *FG promises clearer business rules, new incentives to attract investment *Nigeria’s next reforms to focus on food, power, jobs, business efficiency — Oyedele *Naira stability, rising reserves strengthen economy against shocks — Cardoso *Dangote Group credits reforms for $17bn refinery investment By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor Bangkok, Thailand: The Federal Government has unveiled 65 investment projects requiring a total of $78.5 billion in capital, as it intensifies efforts to attract foreign investors into Nigeria’s energy, transport, agriculture, manufacturing and other critical sectors of the economy. The government, which presented the investment opportunities to foreign investors at an Investors Forum organised by the Nigerian delegation to the ongoing International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said it was developing an investment Deal Room to provide prospective investors with detailed information on projects seeking funding and facilitate investment decisions. Speaking on the initiative, Idris Bellow Osagie, Special Adviser on Economic Strategy to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, is designed to bridge the information gap between project sponsors seeking capital and investors looking for viable opportunities in Nigeria. Osagie urged foreign investors to look beyond concerns about the Nigerian economy and take advantage of the investment opportunities being assembled by the government, insisting that the country was open for business. He explained that the government had consulted federal and state governments, government agencies and private-sector participants to identify transactions requiring financing and assemble the relevant information in a centralised investment platform. According to him, the Deal Room would provide prospective investors with information about projects, including their sponsors, capital requirements, minimum investment thresholds and other financial details needed to assess the opportunities. The objective, he said, was to make it easier for investors to identify projects that matched their investment capacity and interests, obtain further information and engage directly with the relevant project sponsors and government officials. Osagie acknowledged that investors might question some of the economic data and conditions in Nigeria. However, he urged them to assess the investment opportunities available alongside the challenges. He said the government was working to make information on the projects accessible and facilitate meetings between prospective investors and relevant officials. Describing the initiative as part of the government’s efforts to improve investment mobilisation, Osagie urged foreign investors to take a closer look at Nigeria. He said the information on the projects would be updated, while investors could arrange meetings with relevant officials to obtain additional details. The government, he added, was seeking to make it easier for investors to move from identifying opportunities to assessing specific transactions and engaging with project sponsors. Energy, transport dominate $78.5bn pipeline Details of the investment pipeline presented at the forum showed that oil, gas and power projects account for the largest share of the capital requirement, with 25 projects requiring $36.4 billion. Transport and maritime follow with eight projects requiring $25 billion, while agriculture and agro-processing account for six projects requiring $9.8 billion. Industry, manufacturing and mining have 17 projects requiring $6.6 billion, while technology, health and urban services account for nine projects with a combined capital requirement of $700 million. The figures indicate that energy and transport alone account for $61.4 billion, or about 78 per cent of the total investment requirement. The presentation also showed that the 65 projects offer opportunities across different investment sizes, ranging from $1 million to $15 billion. Of the total, 29 projects require less than $100 million each, while 18 require between $100 million and $499 million. One project requires between $500 million and $999 million, while 17 projects require at least $1 billion each. The 17 mega-projects account for $72.3 billion of the overall capital requirement, underscoring the concentration of financing needs among a relatively small number of large transactions. The median capital requirement per project is $153 million, while 48 of the 65 projects require less than $500 million each. The pipeline therefore offers opportunities for investors with different financing capacities, from those interested in relatively small transactions to institutional investors and strategic partners capable of participating in large-scale infrastructure and industrial projects. FG outlines next phase of reforms Meanwhile, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, while speaking at the forum, outlined five priority areas for the next phase of economic reforms, identifying agriculture, power, inflation, regulatory efficiency and data transparency as critical to improving Nigeria’s investment environment. Responding to questions from investors at the forum, Oyedele said the government was developing targeted interventions to address structural problems affecting production, business operations and the cost of living. On agriculture and food inflation, he said the government was examining the underlying causes of rising food prices to ensure that interventions addressed the sources of inflationary pressure. “One of the drivers of inflation is food, so we are now trying to piece it together to find where these problems are coming from,” he said. Oyedele argued that the government needed to distinguish between the factors commonly blamed for inflation and the actual sources of price increases, stressing that policies must be based on evidence. He said the government’s objective was not merely to reduce inflation to single digits but to ensure that it remained at that level. “We know where the inflation and the pressure for it is coming from, and we’re going to tackle it there, not only just to bring it down to a single digit, but to keep it there,” he stated. On the power sector, Oyedele said Nigeria could not achieve its economic ambitions without addressing electricity supply and transmission challenges. “You cannot power a $1 trillion economy in darkness. It’s impossible,” he declared. He said the government was examining strategies to address electricity pricing and transmission constraints, while improving efficiency across the power sector. According to him, resolving the electricity challenge was critical to expanding production, lowering business costs and encouraging new investments. The minister also identified regulatory inefficiency as a major constraint on private-sector investment, arguing that excessive regulations, unclear rules, multiple fees and licensing requirements impose substantial costs on businesses. “We estimate that overregulation, regulatory burden, lack of clarity, and all of those excessive burdens that we put on businesses actually are costing us more than the combined revenue from corporate tax, personal income tax and VAT combined,” he said. Oyedele described regulatory reform as an opportunity to improve the business environment without imposing significant additional costs on the government. “If you ask me, what is the best example of a win-win outcome where the government wins, the private sector wins even more, and it costs the government nearly nothing? It’s solving the problem around regulatory efficiency,” he said. He disclosed that the government had started developing an economic policy framework intended to improve regulatory consistency and prevent the arbitrary introduction of new rules, fees and licences. “So you don’t just wake up one day and introduce a new rule or a new fee or new licenses. No, not anymore,” he stated. The minister also promised improvements in the availability and credibility of fiscal and economic data, saying the government was working to make information more accessible and ensure timely updates. He acknowledged that inconsistent data across government institutions had made it difficult for investors and analysts to assess Nigeria’s economic performance. The Ministry of Finance, he said, was finalising arrangements to publish fiscal data on its website, with commitments to ensure that the information was accessible, credible and regularly updated. FG targets decent jobs, offers new incentives On employment, Oyedele said the government’s priority was to create decent jobs capable of improving living standards rather than focusing solely on the official unemployment rate. “We are clear in our minds that we don’t just need to create jobs; we need to create decent jobs,” he said. He noted that although Nigeria’s official unemployment rate was around five per cent, the poverty rate remained above 50 per cent, indicating that many Nigerians who were working were still struggling financially. “Officially, our unemployment rate is around five per cent and poverty rate is higher than 50 per cent, so you have a lot of working poor,” he stated. The minister said the government was also seeking to make it easier for investors to establish factories and access incentives through the Investment Deal Room. On requests by investors for tax holidays, Oyedele said Nigeria’s reformed tax system had introduced an alternative incentive framework designed to reward qualifying investments. “We’ve transformed our tax system. We have something that is better than a tax holiday. It’s called the Economic Development Incentive, where you get a tax credit,” he said. He explained that the incentive was structured to minimise abuse because investors would have to meet the applicable requirements to qualify for the tax credit. “The good thing about it is it’s hard to abuse, so you have to earn it to get the credit,” he added. Oyedele said the Deal Room would also guide investors through the process of establishing factories and pursuing investment opportunities in the country. “They will show you, they will handhold you, and make it easy for you to do what you have to do,” he said. He further disclosed that the government was working with monetary authorities to improve liquidity and ensure investors could exit naira-denominated investments without additional risk. On taxation of government securities, he said the government was committed to providing clarity so investors could make decisions based on predictable rules. “I cannot guarantee you that there will be no tax, but I can guarantee you there will be clarity so you can price correctly,” he stated. The minister also said the government was engaging the National Bureau of Statistics to improve the timeliness and usefulness of economic data, including information on jobs and producer prices, to support more effective policy decisions. Cardoso links stability to reforms The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, said monetary reforms had helped strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to withstand external shocks, pointing to exchange-rate stability, naira appreciation and improved external reserves. In his remarks at the forum, Cardoso said Nigeria’s external reserves had reached their highest level in 18 years, providing a stronger buffer against global economic headwinds. He argued that the reforms implemented by the authorities had helped prepare the economy to withstand pressures arising from geopolitical tensions and international trade uncertainties. “What we’ve been able to accomplish in terms of having very robust external reserves, highest in 18 years, is also something that affects the ordinary person,” he said. He explained that without the stronger external buffers, Nigeria could have faced some of the pressures confronting other economies, potentially with more severe consequences. Cardoso also linked the relative stability and appreciation of the naira to the reforms, saying the exchange-rate performance had helped cushion the economy against external pressures. “The good thing was that the reforms and the policies were things that were thought through, and we started to implement early enough, such that when those headwinds started to come, not only from the war, but also from the discussions around putting on tariffs, our exchange rate has held stable. In fact, it appreciated,” he said. The CBN governor maintained that exchange-rate stability had broader implications for ordinary Nigerians, even when the benefits were not immediately apparent to households. “What does this mean for me? I’m not feeling it. You do, you definitely feel it. If it wasn’t there, then you would feel it in a very negative way,” he said. Cardoso identified inflation as one of the biggest threats to household welfare, describing it as a tax on the poor because it erodes purchasing power and makes basic goods and services less affordable. “The reason why we felt it was important to give ourselves this as a target is to recognise the fact that inflation is probably the biggest tax on the poor, and so it is critical that we bring it down to levels that are more manageable,” he said. He noted that Nigeria’s inflation rate had declined from about 34 to 35 per cent to around 15 per cent, describing the reduction as significant but insufficient. “I mean, in this instance, inflation has gone from about 34 per cent, 35 per cent to about 15 per cent, and yes, that’s a significant decrease, very significant. But what we are saying basically is that we are not going to rest,” he stated. Cardoso said the medium-term objective remained to bring inflation down to single digits, adding that the CBN’s transition towards inflation targeting would improve transparency and help the public understand the direction of monetary policy. He said the combination of lower inflation, exchange-rate stability and stronger external reserves would help establish a more stable foundation for investment and economic growth. Dangote Group endorses reforms Supporting the government’s investment drive, Hassan Mammud, Group Chief Economist, Dangote Group, said the consistency and credibility of Nigeria’s fiscal and monetary policies had helped restore investor confidence and improve the operating environment for businesses. Mammud, who represented the Dangote Group at the forum, said the reforms had helped the conglomerate overcome difficulties associated with the previous economic environment and improve its ability to plan and make investment decisions. He said the transparency and credibility of monetary policy had significantly improved the group’s capacity to make projections and stabilise its operations, particularly in relation to its investment of about $17 billion in the Dangote Refinery. “The transparency and the credibility we have seen in that has significantly enabled the Dangote Group to have good projections and was able to come out of the woods from his investment of about $17 billion dollars in the refinery,” he said. “That cannot happen in an economy where there are no consistencies, where there are no credibility of fiscal and monetary policy, and also the incentives that goes with operating in an export-free zone.” Mammud described the group’s experience as a confidence-builder for prospective investors considering Nigeria and other African countries, arguing that investment decisions depended not only on market opportunities but also on the credibility of government policies and the regulatory environment. He urged foreign investors to take advantage of the opportunities available in Nigeria. “Please come into Nigeria, bring your investment. Nigeria is actually a symbol to other African countries now,” he said. Mammud also cited the Dangote Group’s investment expansion into Kenya as an indication of the potential for Nigerian businesses to support industrial development across Africa. He stressed that investors needed to be bold, but added that such boldness depended on credible policies and regulatory reforms. Investor protections, incentives To strengthen the investment proposition, the presentation outlined several protections and incentives available to foreign investors. These include permission for 100 per cent foreign ownership in most sectors and full repatriation of capital and profits, subject to obtaining a Certificate of Capital Importation. The government also highlighted 17 double-taxation agreements and 13 bilateral investment treaties, alongside Nigeria’s membership of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID). Under the incentives presented, qualifying capital expenditure may attract a tax credit of five per cent per annum for five years through the Economic Development Tax Incentive. The measures are intended to address investor concerns about ownership, returns, taxation and investment protection. Interested investors were encouraged to review the 65 project profiles available through the online investment directory and the Projects Nigeria Special Edition, which provide details of project sponsors, deal structures and scorecards. Osagie also encouraged investors to visit the Deal Room office, where Ministry of Finance officials and Nigerian business leaders could provide further information on individual projects. items.title: President Mahama urges churches to provide safe spaces for children and vulnerable people
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged religious bodies, particularly churches, to provide safe spaces for children and vulnerable people. Addressing the ongoing World Assemblies of God Congress 2026 in Accra, the President said churches must uphold the trust placed in them as places of safety. He called on religious institutions to ensure that people seeking refuge and support within their communities receive protection and care. “Let us all be mentors to our younger generation. Let us be mentors who listen, offer opportunities to serve and set an example of integrity that these young people can follow. The church should also be a safe place for children and vulnerable people,” he said. He added, “Spiritual authority entails a duty of care; we must safeguard that trust through responsible conduct, clear conduct and accountability.” The President’s appeal came at the opening of the three-day congress, which runs until 16 October under the theme, “Commissioned: One Mandate, Every Nation”. The programme includes plenary sessions, workshops and revival rallies, with the opening session held at the Grand Arena of the Accra International Conference Centre. The gathering is the 10th Triennial World Assemblies of God Fellowship Congress and marks the first time the event has been hosted in Africa. It brings together church leaders and ministers to discuss the Church’s mission and its role in communities worldwide. Ahead of the congress, the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Ghana, Rev. Stephen Yenusom Wengam, said organisers expected more than 10,000 participants from about 100 countries.

items.title: Éducation à Kankan : un déficit de 736 enseignants, la DPE lance un cri d’alarme
items.description: À Kankan, le manque d’enseignants perturbe le fonctionnement de plusieurs établissements scolaires, particulièrement dans l’enseignement élémentaire. Face à cette situation, le directeur préfectoral de l’Éducation, Souleymane Daffé, appelle les autorités à agir rapidement pour combler le déficit, alors que l’année scolaire 2026 a démarré le 5 octobre sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Selon les données communiquées par le directeur préfectoral de l’Éducation (DPE), les besoins en personnel enseignant dans la préfecture sont estimés à 736 enseignants, dont 630 pour l’élémentaire et 106 pour le secondaire . Cette insuffisance s’explique notamment par l’augmentation des effectifs scolaires, les départs à la retraite et les décès d’enseignants. Une situation que les recrutements effectués jusque-là ne permettent pas de compenser, selon Souleymane Daffé. « Après l’engagement de 2024, il n’y a pas eu d’autre recrutement. Chaque année, des enseignants partent à la retraite, tandis que le nombre d’élèves scolarisés augmente. S’il n’y a pas de recrutement pour remplacer ceux qui partent, le besoin en enseignants se fait forcément sentir », explique-t-il. D’après les statistiques présentées par le responsable préfectoral, les établissements scolaires relevant de la DPE de Kankan, y compris ceux des localités récemment rattachées à son ressort, notamment Tokounou et Sabadou-Baranama, comptent actuellement 2 223 enseignants en activité . Cet effectif se répartit entre 1 361 enseignants dans l’enseignement élémentaire et 862 dans le secondaire. Malgré ces ressources humaines, le déficit reste important et affecte particulièrement les écoles primaires. Dans certaines localités rurales, la situation est préoccupante : des établissements disposant de quatre classes ne comptent parfois qu’un ou deux enseignants pour assurer les cours. « Tous les enseignants ne sont pas au complet, surtout à l’élémentaire. Il y a des villages où, pour quatre classes, on ne dispose souvent que d’un ou deux enseignants », déplore Souleymane Daffé. Des solutions locales pour maintenir les cours Face à cette pénurie, les responsables éducatifs tentent de limiter les conséquences sur les apprentissages. La DPE privilégie notamment une gestion locale des difficultés, sans procéder à des permutations d’enseignants qui pourraient, selon son directeur, aggraver le déficit dans certaines écoles. Dans plusieurs localités, les Associations des parents et amis de l’école (APAE) apportent également leur contribution au maintien des activités pédagogiques. Elles prennent notamment en charge des enseignants contractuels pour renforcer les équipes en poste. Souleymane Daffé salue cette mobilisation communautaire, qui permet de soutenir les établissements confrontés au manque de personnel. Il souligne toutefois que cet appui ne saurait constituer une réponse durable aux besoins de la préfecture. L’espoir placé dans le recrutement de 6 000 enseignants Pour réduire le déficit, la DPE mise désormais sur le recrutement annoncé de 6 000 enseignants au niveau national dans la fonction publique. Selon Souleymane Daffé, cette opération pourrait contribuer à améliorer la situation à Kankan, même si elle ne permettra pas nécessairement de combler tous les besoins. Le directeur préfectoral appelle ainsi les autorités compétentes à accélérer le processus de recrutement et d’affectation afin que les établissements les plus touchés puissent bénéficier rapidement de nouveaux enseignants. « Nous avons un grand espoir avec le recrutement annoncé. Cela ne corrigera pas définitivement le déficit, mais permettra de réduire les besoins. Nous demandons à l’État d’accélérer les choses, car l’année scolaire a déjà commencé. Un retard supplémentaire d’un à deux mois dans la mise à disposition des enseignants risque d’entraîner des retards dans les programmes scolaires », prévient-il. Alors que les cours ont repris depuis le 5 octobre 2027, le renforcement du personnel enseignant demeure un défi majeur pour la DPE de Kankan. La rapidité des recrutements et des affectations sera déterminante pour améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage, notamment dans les zones rurales où le manque d’enseignants compromet déjà le bon déroulement des cours.

items.title: Tunisian journalists fear jail again as freedoms erode
items.description: By Tarek Amara TUNIS, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Journalists in Tunisia who enjoyed a burst of press freedom after the 2011 Arab Spring are once again looking over their shoulders in the knowledge their work may land them in prison. The 2011 overthrow of autocrat Zine El-Abidine Ben Ali unshackled Tunisia's media, but a decade later President Kais Saied's seizure of sweeping powers began eroding those gains.

items.title: George Dadzie Junior highly tipped in NDC regional secretary race due to grassroots experience
items.description: George Dadzie Junior, a former Western Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), is seeking to become the party’s next Western Regional Secretary, with supporters pointing to his experience in party organisation, grassroots mobilisation and member engagement as key strengths. As the party prepares for its regional elections next month, his backers believe his previous leadership role has given him an understanding of the NDC’s organisational structures and the challenges facing the party in the region. Yaw Asomaning, an NDC activist, said hard work was one of the qualities associated with Dadzie Junior’s political career. According to him, Dadzie Junior is regarded by many supporters as a committed party activist who understands the importance of grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with members. His supporters believe these qualities would be useful in the Regional Secretary role, which involves coordinating party activities and maintaining communication between regional leadership and the party’s structures. Experience in party organisation Dadzie Junior’s tenure as Western Regional Youth Organiser is another aspect of his candidature highlighted by supporters. They argue that the experience exposed him to grassroots organisation, mobilisation and the coordination required to sustain party activities. Ali Mahad, a long-standing party member, also pointed to his previous experience as relevant to his bid for the position. His backers further cite his interpersonal skills and ability to engage people from different backgrounds, arguing that these could help him work with regional executives, constituency officers and branch members. Samad Sulemana said the Regional Secretary’s role required administrative competence, coordination and the ability to work effectively with other party executives. Supporters believe Dadzie Junior’s relationship-building skills could help promote cooperation within the regional administration. Focus on unity and members’ welfare Party unity and the welfare of grassroots members also feature in the case being made for Dadzie Junior. His supporters say he recognises the need for party members to feel included in decision-making and for their concerns to be addressed beyond election periods. They also cite his willingness to support colleagues and his tolerance of differing views as qualities that could help manage disagreements within the party. In a contest involving aspirants with different support bases, they argue, the ability to listen to opposing views and encourage dialogue would be important in maintaining cohesion. His backers also point to his character and discipline, saying the Regional Secretary must be able to defend the party’s interests while respecting its constitution and established procedures. Delegates to decide The NDC’s Western Regional Secretary contest will test the appeal of the aspirants and their ability to convince delegates of their suitability for the position. For Dadzie Junior’s supporters, his previous leadership experience, knowledge of grassroots politics and emphasis on cooperation make him a credible contender. Ultimately, however, the outcome will depend on the choices of delegates as the party selects its next regional leadership.

items.title: AI could cause 'major' incidents within 2 years without safeguards, says Google DeepMind chair
items.description: Artificial intelligence systems could cause “major” security incidents within two years without adequate steps to make them safe as capabilities grow, Google’s DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis said on Wednesday. Speaking at an AI conference in Dublin, Hassabis described recent incidents as “early warning shots” fired by systems that “aren’t that powerful yet”. “So the incidents aren’t that major,” he said. “But they could be, looking into next year and the next couple of years, if we don’t do more work as an industry and individually as companies and governments on securing these systems,” Hassabis warned. Concerns about AI safety have soared after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology. Hassabis said new AI models should probably first be tested in offline “sandboxes”, after other companies’ models escaped the closed environments used to assess their capabilities. The European Union’s tech chief, Henna Virkkunen, said AI firms needed to invest more time into testing their systems to retain control over them. “The competition is so hard globally that it seems that all the companies, they are not investing enough time and resources really to test their models,” Virkkunen told reporters as she arrived at the Dublin summit. “They have to be able to control… these systems,” she said, noting that the European Union has sent information requests to all major AI companies asking what safety and security measures they have in place. The European Commission gained new regulatory powers in August under the AI Act, the world’s most far-reaching rules to curb potentially dangerous uses of the technology.
